reason: The text repeatedly emphasizes and reinforces strict hierarchy. Pharaoh holds supreme authority over his servants and officials, summoning his magicians and wise men to interpret dreams. Joseph is elevated to the position of second-in-command over all Egypt, with explicit statements that 'without you, no one will lift his hand or foot' (v. 44). The text validates this hierarchical structure—Joseph is given symbols of authority (fine linen, gold necklace, second chariot), an Egyptian name, and a wife. All of Egypt is instructed to obey Joseph's commands (v. 40), and his hierarchical authority is used to implement the famine preparations. The narrative presents this strict hierarchy as not only important but essential to the survival and administration of Egypt.
